title: Book One · Chapter 118: Keep the Picture at Home
story:
Mr Qiu looks at the drawing again. He looks for a long time. He checked the books. Then he agreed to talk. Now Ronan has brought the drawing to him.

They are sitting at the kitchen table. Mum is outside with Mrs Lan. Ronan has brought the paper himself. He has not shown it to anyone at school.

“The roof is very dark,” Mr Qiu says.

“It was dark that day.”

“Yes.”

Ronan waits for him to read the words.

Mr Qiu reads them. Then he puts the paper on the table.

“I don't want this story on a wall.”

“It says people can help.”

“It also says things about my money.”

Ronan looks at his own writing. He wrote: Mr Qiu lost his books. He also wrote: Mr Qiu needs help. He drew a box for people to write their names. He heard some things from other people. He guessed the rest himself.

“You have to pay for the roof,” he says.

“The place belongs to another man. I must talk with him about the roof. We have some things to agree on. You do not know all of them.”

“I could put a question mark there.”

Mr Qiu's mouth moves, almost a smile.

“A very large question mark would still be on a wall.”

Ronan rubs the edge of the paper. He wants Mr Qiu to like his picture. He also wants to put it away at once.

“May I keep the roof?” he asks.

“In your drawing?”

“Yes. Without the money.”

“Let me see that one when it is done.”

It is not a yes. Ronan hears that now.

He takes a clean sheet. On one side he draws the old stall. On the other side he draws the two crates. He leaves room between them.

“What can I write?”

“You can write this: My pencils are in a dry place.”

“That is very short.”

“My pencils are short too. They still work.”

Ronan laughs. He writes the line. Under it he writes Mr Qiu's name, then stops.

“Do you want your name here?”

“Yes. Qiu. Not the poor old man by the wet roof.”

Ronan's ears grow warm. He has not used those words. But his story may make people think that. He looks at his line about help.

He turns the first sheet over. Mr Qiu watches him.

“You can keep a drawing for yourself,” he says. “That does not mean everyone at school may see it.”

“I can put this one away.”

“You can. Or change it.”

Ronan folds it along the old line. Then he folds it again. He puts it under his own book.

Mum comes in to get a bowl. She sees the new sheet.

“Did you finish?”

“Not yet,” Ronan says. “Both of us must like this one.”

Mr Qiu lifts one finger.

“Three. Those are Mrs Lan's crates now.”

“They are your crates,” Mum says.

“Her room makes them look better.”

Mrs Lan calls from the yard. “My room looks better without those crates!” Mr Qiu laughs at last. Ronan draws the wall behind the crates. Now people can see the crates beside the wall.

Then he asks Mr Qiu, “Where should I draw your chair?” The old man points to the dry side. Ronan puts it there. He gives the chair four legs this time. In the first picture he gave it three, and the old man looked ready to fall.

“Better,” Mr Qiu says. “I would like to stay on my chair.”

---

重点表达：question mark＝问号；put away＝收起；for yourself＝给自己。

情节提示：roof＝屋顶；fold＝折叠；guess＝猜测。

理解：1. Mr Qiu 不愿公开哪些内容？2. Ronan 为什么重新画一张图？
